::: {.solutions}

**20 questions.** Suggested time: **90 minutes**, no calculator.

Every question comes from a TMUA past paper, a MAT paper or a TMUA mock, and its source is shown beside the
question number. None of them appears in the S1 class questions.

For every question the method is the same: **rewrite the sentence as "if … then …" first**, then read off
which way the arrow points. Do not try to reason about the meaning in English, because that is how arrows get
flipped by accident.

| Section | What it covers | Questions |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Reading an implication** | testing implications, counterexamples, contrapositives | 1–6 |
| **B — "Exactly one is true"** | translating options, then eliminating | 7–12 |
| **C — "If and only if" and "only if"** | exact conditions, and using a definition in both directions | 13–17 |
| **D — Sufficient and necessary** | the link between the forms and necessary / sufficient | 18–20 |

---

# Section A — Reading an implication

## Question 1 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">Tyler TMUA Set D · P2 Q9</span>

::: {.question}
A set of cards has a single letter printed on the front and a single number printed on the back.

Five of these cards are laid on the table so that only one side of each card is visible. The cards show:

$$5 \qquad \text{E} \qquad 7 \qquad \text{F} \qquad 9$$

Lara states that all cards with a vowel on the front have a prime number on the back.

Which cards do you need to turn over in order to check if this statement is true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** all of the cards

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** cards E, 5 and 7

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** card E only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** cards F and 9

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** cards E and 9
:::

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** If $\mathrm f(x)\ge\mathrm g(x)$ for all $x\ge0$, then $\mathrm f'(x)\ge\mathrm g'(x)$ for all $x\ge0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** If $\mathrm f'(x)\ge\mathrm g'(x)$ for all $x\ge0$, then $\mathrm f(x)\ge\mathrm g(x)$ for all $x\ge0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** none of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** I only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** I and II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** I and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** II and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** I, II and III
:::

## Question 6 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">JZ Maths Mock B · P2 Q18</span>

::: {.question}
Let $f$ and $g$ be polynomials. Consider the following four statements.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** If $f'(x)\ge g'(x)$ for all $x\ge0$ and $f(0)\ge g(0)$, then $f(x)\ge g(x)$ for all $x\ge0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** If $f(x)\ge g(x)$ for all $x\ge0$, then $\displaystyle\int_0^x t\,f(t)\,dt\ge\int_0^x t\,g(t)\,dt$ for all $x\ge0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** If $\displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\,dt\ge\int_0^x g(t)\,dt$ for all $x\ge0$, then $f(x)\ge g(x)$ for all $x\ge0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**IV** If $\displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\,dt\ge\int_0^x g(t)\,dt$ for all $x\ge0$, then $\displaystyle\int_0^x t^2f(t)\,dt\ge\int_0^x t^2g(t)\,dt$ for all $x\ge0$.

Which of the statements are true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** None of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** I only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** IV only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** I and II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** II and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** I and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** all except I

&nbsp;&nbsp;**J** all except II

&nbsp;&nbsp;**K** all except III

&nbsp;&nbsp;**L** all except IV
:::

::: {.workspace style="min-height:10cm"}

:::

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** This jar contains more than £3 and less than £6

## Question 8 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">JZ Maths Mock C · P2 Q7</span>

::: {.question}
Six sealed black bags are labelled $P,Q,R,S,T$ and $U$. Each bag contains the same number of balls. This number is a non-zero whole number from $3$ to $8$ inclusive.

Each bag has a label with a statement written on it. The statement may be true or false.

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $P$: "The number of balls in this bag is a multiple of $3$."

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $Q$: "The number of balls in this bag is even."

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $R$: "The number of balls in this bag is prime."

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $S$: "The number of balls in this bag is at most $4$."

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $T$: "The number of balls in this bag is at least $7$."

&nbsp;&nbsp;Bag $U$: "The number of balls in this bag is a perfect square."

Given that exactly one of the six statements is true, which bag has the true statement on its label?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $P$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $Q$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $R$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $S$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $T$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $U$
:::

## Question 11 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">JZ Maths Mock D · P2 Q19</span>

::: {.question}
Let $f$ be a function defined on the real numbers. Consider the following seven statements, each intended to hold for all real values of $a$:

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(1)** $f(a)>0$ if $a>0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(2)** $a>0$ is necessary for $f(a)>0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(3)** $a\le0$ only if $f(a)\le0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(4)** If $f(a)\le0$, then $a\le0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(5)** $f(a)>0$ whenever $a\le0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(6)** $a>0$ is sufficient for $f(a)>0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(7)** $f(a)\le0$ is sufficient and necessary for $a>0$.

Given that exactly one of these seven statements is true for the particular function $f$ in question, which one is it?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** Statement (1)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** Statement (2)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** Statement (3)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** Statement (4)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** Statement (5)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** Statement (6)

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** Statement (7)
:::

::: {.workspace style="min-height:8cm"}

## Question 12 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">JZ Maths Mock E · P2 Q12</span>

::: {.question}
Let $f$ be a function. Each of the following is a statement about all real numbers $a$ (for instance, the first reads: for every $a$, if $f(x)>0$ for all $x>a$, then $f(a)<0$). Exactly one of them is true.

Which one is it?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $f(x)>0$ for all $x>a$ **only if** $f(a)<0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $f(a)<0$ and $f(x)>0$ for all $x>a$ **cannot both** hold

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $f(x)>0$ for all $x>a$ is **necessary** for $f(a)<0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** if $f(a)\ge0$ then $f(x)\le0$ for some $x>a$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $f(x)>0$ for all $x>a$ **implies** $f(a)\ge0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $f(a)\ge0$ **if and only if** $f(x)\le0$ for some $x>a$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** $f(a)<0$ is **sufficient** for there to exist $x>a$ with $f(x)\le0$
:::

## Question 16 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2018 · P2 Q17</span>

::: {.question}
A positive integer is called a *squaresum* **if and only if** it can be written as the sum of the squares of two integers. For example, $61$ and $9$ are both squaresums since $61=5^2+6^2$ and $9=3^2+0^2$.

A prime number is called *awkward* **if and only if** it has a remainder of $3$ when divided by $4$. For example, $23$ is awkward since $23=5\times4+3$.

A (true) theorem due to Fermat states that:

> A positive integer is a squaresum **if and only if** each of its awkward prime factors occurs to an even power in its prime factorisation.

It follows that $5\times23^2$ is a squaresum, since $23$ occurs to the power $2$, but $5\times23^3$ is not, since $23$ occurs to the power $3$.

Which one of the following statements is **not** true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** Every square number is a squaresum.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** If $N$ and $M$ are squaresums, then so is $NM$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** If $NM$ is a squaresum, then $N$ and $M$ are squaresums.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** If $N$ is not a squaresum, then $kN$ is a squaresum for some number $k$ which is a product of awkward primes.
:::

::: {.workspace style="min-height:8cm"}
Working
:::

## Question 17 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2023 · P2 Q20</span>

::: {.question}
Let $f$ be a polynomial with real coefficients.

The integral $I_{p,q}$, where $p<q$, is defined by

$$I_{p,q}=\int_p^q\big(f(x)\big)^2-\big(f(\lvert x\rvert)\big)^2\,dx$$

Which of the following statements must be true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**1** $I_{p,q}=0$ **only if** $0<p$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**2** $f'(x)<0$ for all $x$ **only if** $I_{p,q}<0$ for all $p<q<0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**3** $I_{p,q}>0$ **only if** $p<0$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** none of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** 1 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** 2 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** 3 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** 1 and 2 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** 1 and 3 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** 2 and 3 only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** 1, 2 and 3
:::

Working

## Question 20 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">Tyler TMUA Set B · P2 Q8</span>

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** The condition $p(a)p(b)<0$ is not necessary and not sufficient for $(*)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** The condition $p(a)p(b)<0$ is necessary but not sufficient for $(*)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** The condition $p(a)p(b)<0$ is sufficient but not necessary for $(*)$
